name: Kanauta

queries.query: Kanauta Jaipur Rajasthan official cadastral parcel map land records GIS
queries.result: First-party discovery identified Rajasthan Government Apna Khata/e-Dharti and Bhu-Naksha land-record services, the Rajdharaa Urban GIS portal with Khasra layers, and official Jaipur Development Authority planning material for Kanota. The sources establish a Rajasthan/Jaipur cadastral and planning service lead, but no anonymous parcel ID-plus-geometry response was obtained.

queries.query: कानौटा जयपुर राजस्थान आधिकारिक भू नक्शा भू अभिलेख
queries.result: Hindi first-party discovery identified Rajasthan Government Apna Khata, its भू नक्शा link, the Board of Revenue cadastral-map digitization pages, and official Kanota planning material. These evidence the state land-record custodian and Jaipur planning context; they do not provide a verified anonymous parcel geometry response for the preserved WUP point.

registryEvidence.custodian: Government of Rajasthan Board of Revenue / Apna Khata (e-Dharti) and Rajasthan cadastral-map services; Jaipur Development Authority for the Kanota planning context
registryEvidence.scopeNote: Apna Khata identifies Rajasthan Revenue Board land-record services and links Bhu-Naksha. Rajdharaa states that its Urban GIS uses khasra and village boundaries from the Settlement Department. JDA publishes an official Kanota land-use plan. This evidences state and local planning/map custodianship, not open citywide parcel-vector completeness.

parcelDiscovery.source: Rajasthan Bhu-Naksha / Apna Khata and Rajdharaa Urban GIS
parcelDiscovery.note: The exact WUP point was preserved in latitude/longitude order and was not shifted. No safe native parcel identity or unchanged polygon was returned, so no GeoJSON sample is retained.

requestOutcomes.outcome: Official Rajasthan Revenue Board landing page retrieved by first-party web inspection; it identifies Apna Khata/e-Dharti and links भू नक्शा.

Official Urban GIS HTML retrieved; it exposes Khasra, plot, and location-oriented UI and states that khasra/village boundaries come from the Settlement Department. No feature response or schema was obtained.

Official Bhu-Naksha viewer discovery result identified; web fetch returned HTTP 502 Bad Gateway and a direct curl request timed out after 30 seconds. No login, token, CAPTCHA/Cloudflare bypass, or TLS exception was used.
Official JDA Kanota land-use-plan result identified; fetch was not used as parcel geometry and the web reader reported content too large. This is planning evidence only.
Official Board of Revenue cadastral-map digitization page identified through Hindi discovery; no parcel feature endpoint was exposed in the bounded inspection.

safeFieldAllowlist: stable native parcel identifier only if source-proven
uncertainty: The queue spelling is Kanauta; official JDA material and discovery results use Kanota, so locality-name equivalence is treated as a lead, not as a coordinate adjustment.
The Bhu-Naksha viewer was unavailable through bounded anonymous retrieval in this workspace; no parcel absence is inferred from the timeout or HTTP 502.
The Rajdharaa viewer documents Khasra layers and public viewing disclaimers, but its current JavaScript/API route and schema were not qualified.
No owner, address, contact, titleholder, personal, tax/account, certificate, or other unsafe fields were requested or retained.
Independent serial review is required before any adapter or runtime qualification.
